manifest.topic: Reading simple sentences with short vowel words
manifest.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

curatorBrief.title: Adventures in Reading Short Vowel Sentences
curatorBrief.intent: Welcome first-grade learners to the world of reading decodable sentences! Introduce the five short vowel sounds (/a/, /e/, /i/, /o/, /u/), demonstrate how to blend these sounds with consonants into simple CVC words, and inspire students to read complete decodable sentences aloud with accuracy and confidence.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Identify the short vowel sounds in simple three-letter words

components.title: Meet the Five Short Vowels
components.intent: Introduce the five short vowel phonemes (/a/ in cat, /e/ in bed, /i/ in pig, /o/ in fox, /u/ in sun) with clear visual diagrams and audio cues, allowing students to explore each short vowel in CVC words one at a time.

components.title: Say the Short Vowel Sounds
components.intent: Provide live-judged spoken practice for producing short vowel sounds. The tutor models the pure short vowel sound and keyword, then listens as the student isolates and speaks the sound aloud into the microphone.

components.title: Match the Middle Vowel Sound
components.intent: Engage students in spoken medial sound discrimination: students listen to target CVC words and name the matching word with the identical short vowel sound (e.g., matching the short /a/ in 'bat' to 'cap').

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Apply letter-sound blending to read short vowel words

components.title: Blend Sounds Into Words
components.intent: Guide students through interactive sound-by-sound blending using visual phoneme tiles. Tap each tile to hear its sound, then blend the sounds continuously across three-letter CVC patterns to reveal rewarding illustrations.

components.title: Read CVC Words Aloud
components.intent: Offer live-judged Direct Instruction word decoding where students cold-read printed short vowel CVC words aloud (e.g., 'cat', 'hop', 'red', 'rug', 'pin') with immediate audio feedback from the tutor.

components.title: Word Workout and Meaning Match
components.intent: Challenge students to solidify CVC decoding automaticity through word chains and matching decoded short-vowel words to their corresponding picture representations.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Read simple sentences containing short vowel words with fluency

components.title: Build Short Vowel Sentences
components.intent: Let students construct decodable simple sentences by arranging color-coded tiles consisting of CVC words and familiar high-frequency sight words (e.g., 'The fat cat sat on a mat').

components.title: Read Sentences Aloud
components.intent: Facilitate live-judged sentence reading where the student decodes printed 3-6 word decodable sentences containing short vowel words and basic sight words aloud, with word-by-word accuracy validation by the tutor.

components.title: Read Connected Sentences and Check Understanding
components.intent: Present a short controlled-vocabulary decodable text line-by-line for students to decode aloud, followed by spoken comprehension checks confirming understanding of the simple sentences read.

finalAssessment.title: Short Vowel Sentence Reading Checkpoint
finalAssessment.intent: Assess student mastery across all three objectives by prompting them to identify middle vowel sounds, decode target CVC words, and match simple decodable sentences to the correct picture context.

diagram.description: A clear educational word chart showing three 3-letter words (CAT, PIG, POT) with the middle short vowel in each word highlighted.
diagram.imagePrompt: Educational schematic chart displaying three three-letter CVC words: 'CAT', 'PIG', and 'POT'. Each word is displayed in three distinct wooden toy letter blocks. The middle vowel letter of each word is brightly highlighted with glowing colored borders: 'A' in CAT in red, 'I' in PIG in blue, and 'O' in POT in amber. Labeled arrows point to the middle letter of each word showing its short vowel sound. Clean minimalist classroom graphic, dark navy background, crisp white consonant letters, bold colored vowels.

concepts.name: Short A Sound
concepts.briefDefinition: The quick vowel sound that says /æ/, heard in the middle of words like 'cat'.
concepts.diagramHighlight: The highlighted red letter 'A' in the middle block of the word 'CAT'

inContext.scenario: When you put on a baseball cap to go outside on a sunny day...
inContext.whereToFind: The short 'a' is the middle /æ/ sound heard inside the word 'cap'.

selfCheck.prompt: Which three-letter word has the short 'a' sound in the middle?
selfCheck.hint: Listen for the /æ/ sound, just like in 'apple' or 'cat'.

concepts.name: Short I Sound
concepts.briefDefinition: The quick vowel sound that says /ɪ/, heard in the middle of words like 'pig'.
concepts.diagramHighlight: The highlighted blue letter 'I' in the middle block of the word 'PIG'

inContext.scenario: When you take a tiny sip of cold water through a straw...
inContext.whereToFind: The short 'i' is the middle /ɪ/ sound heard inside the word 'sip'.

selfCheck.prompt: Which three-letter word has the short 'i' sound in the middle?
selfCheck.hint: Listen for the /ɪ/ sound, just like at the start of 'igloo'.

concepts.name: Short O Sound
concepts.briefDefinition: The quick vowel sound that says /ɒ/, heard in the middle of words like 'pot'.
concepts.diagramHighlight: The highlighted amber letter 'O' in the middle block of the word 'POT'

inContext.scenario: When a tiny green frog jumps across the grass, it makes a hop.
inContext.whereToFind: The short 'o' is the middle /ɒ/ sound you say in the word 'hop'.

selfCheck.prompt: Which three-letter word has the short 'o' sound in the middle?
selfCheck.hint: Listen for the open /ɒ/ sound, just like at the start of 'octopus'.

problems.question: Which picture has the short a sound?
problems.rationale: The word cat has the short a sound heard in apple. The words bed, hen, and net all have the short e sound.
problems.teachingNote: Have emerging readers isolate the middle vowel sound aloud to contrast /æ/ in cat with /ɛ/ in bed.
successCriteria: Identify the short a vowel sound in simple three-letter words
Distinguish between short a and short e vowel sounds
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.rationale: The short i sound completes the CVC word big. Short vowels are essential for early decoding and reading fluency.
problems.teachingNote: Remind students to look at the surrounding letters to choose the correct vowel sound.
successCriteria: Identify the short vowel sound in a simple three-letter word
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.question: Which word matches the sounds /p/ /o/ /t/?
problems.rationale: The sounds /p/, /o/, and /t/ blend together to make pot. The letter o makes the short /o/ sound in the middle.
problems.teachingNote: Encourage emerging readers to tap each sound with their fingers before blending them smoothly together.
successCriteria: Blend individual phonemes to decode a short vowel CVC word.
Distinguish the short o sound from other short vowel sounds in print.
problems.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS

problems.prompt: Match each word to its clue.
problems.rationale: Each short vowel word matches its simple clue. Blending letter sounds helps readers connect words to their meanings.
problems.teachingNote: Remind students to tap out individual sounds (/s/ /u/ /n/) before matching with the meaning.
successCriteria: Blend letter sounds to read CVC short vowel words.
Connect decodable words to their simple meanings.

problems.teachingNote: Prompt emerging readers to point to the word 'cat' in the first sentence and look at the action word that comes right after it.
